I answered B from domain knowledge plus the correlations. I did not run a causal-discovery test.

The two variables are moderately negatively correlated (r ≈ −0.27). Correlation alone doesn't give a direction. Physically, sea-level pressure is a large-scale circulation variable. Pressure patterns drive moisture convergence and ascent, which in turn shape cloud water. The reverse, cloud water changing sea-level pressure, is not a plausible mechanism. A double-sided relationship is also unlikely, and the nonzero correlation rules out D.

ANSWER: B
